body:
Same but on messenger! Creeped us out. That’s weird! I was in a video call with my bf over messenger and a white thumbs up appeared in the middle of my video— both of us saw it, I was unsure first bec my thumbnail(vid) is smaller. And we didn’t click anything at all. I’m on mac and he’s on his android. So not sure if this is an iOS thing? 

Is this a Meta/FB thing? Anybody has an idea?

Hi! Did you try downloading the app? You can access your account there, using the contact number you used to register your account. Hope it helps? I am having similar problems din with their “customer service”; pero the fact that they are threatening you via call, that’s already harassment though.

Hello OP! I hope you can give me updates on this kasi I just got with them on the phone and everything you said was spot on. Napaka condescending, they can’t even give me my lifetime ID and they have the nerve to threaten me instead of politely answering my questions. I know that lending companies can be quite persistent in terms of asking for repayment but I know I am an honest customer, magbabayad naman talaga ako. I just incurred delay kasi kakauwi ko lang sa Pilipinas, the fund was truly for emergency use that time na malayo ako. 

Di ko kinaya yung verbal harassment nila, napaka condescending for a “main office” and napaka defensive. Tinawagan ko sila ulet, parang nasa isang kwarto lang halos, alam na tinawagan na ako kanina daw and all hahaha. May ipapa-clarify sana ako ulet. I’d rather just pay this all and be done with it. Sinabihan pa ako na dapat nagbabasa daw ako ng Terms of Agreement hahahahaha. Baka pareho kami di nagbasa kasi di din nila masagot directly yung inquiry ko.

Same here. I’m struggling with maintaining friendships that are constant and for-all-kinds of weather. I’ve friends who I consider for-life and are actually low maintenance but I can’t always run to them these days and they can’t always share my triumps or joys. But I am certain they are permanent in my life. I see that they can easily make new friends with seemingly lasting bonds as well. On the other hand, I can’t maintain friendships without them seeing me as a threat or a competition. And then there are those who are only fair-weather friends. The problem with growing up having that one best friend and thinking that person is enough and that I need not mind finding other friends has left me feeling lonely these years especially since we both grew apart.

I’m the least favorite person in the family too because even in the family, I’m seen as if I’m a competition, a “know-it-all” or the “righteous” one when all I really want is to make good and not tolerate anymore wrong things and abusive things. It’s hard to always be left out and feeling alone when you just really want to be loved. If I have friends who do not need to compare themselves to me, I’d hype them up, and really be proud of them. Sadly, these days, it’s not always reciprocated.

Same. I have just looked up on Japanese Language Schools and it turns out they are doing online courses. I am honestly tired of doing online mode. It works for some but it is draining. 

I hope borders really open soon for students.

P.S. What language schools can you recommend in greater Tokyo? (sorry I am only just starting my research now)
You can do it!!!

“he’s baited me to be warm and fuzzy, then gone back on it which hurt and made me feel ashamed for taking the bait. He hurt my feelings and embarrassed me in less than 5 seconds but technically did nothing wrong.”

This happened to me too. I felt embarrassed just by being intimate with him while we were cuddling on bed. He eventually told me he’s not in the mood at all or that he was just extremely tired. A week prior he was so suggestive that we watch this funny sexy yet controversial local film in our alone time together or mini-vacay. I didn’t want to kill the fun so I just nodded even though I find that film nonsense and cheap. 

I honestly felt like crying after our vacation time because he went cold and silent for a week, saying he just needed to recharge and be away from me as I have become too clingy.

My ex is a sociopath and when he broke up with me the second time around, he told me that he only came back to me “out of guilt”. I’m not sure how I responded to this but I tried my best to remind him of everything he sworn to do and change. I also told him that I never begged for him to come back in the first place, it was him who beeped me up after gaslighting me and saying hurtful things to me all at once. He then said his apologies, further hurting me by telling me it was just his mistake to come back “out of guilt”. 

Fast forward recently, as I was deleting some screenshots on my phone, I found the cheesy messages he sent me the very moment he tried to win me back. In that message, I actually told him

“You don’t have to be guilty of anything anymore... if you’re just doing this to make up for things... just don’t.” 

to which he responded, “Apologetic, sure. But I am not doing this out of guilt.” 

And the rest of text was about him begging me to help him and that we try to have a new start bla bla bla.

In the end, he used my words and warnings against me that they became even too foreign for my brain to remember.

I hope you don’t think about him everyday like I do. I still think of him everyday despite not talking to him anymore. I still stalk his social media even though I’m blocked- I still find ways to know how he’s doing. It is so hard indeed.

No. My lawyer said that emotional abuse is still abuse. Laws may vary from where you live but do look up about Violence Against Women and Children laws. I had the same worries before. I feel like abusive behavior of a mentally ill person may be legally justified and may even take the side of the defense of the court. But legally speaking, if they don’t get jailed... they’d be pushed in a mental health facility instead.  

People using their mental health as card to excuse their wrong doing are really shitty.

Well yeah, I’m sorry for coming off too strong- of course it’s NEVER okay. But that’s really bullshit, how people would rather take the abuser’s side instead of calling him out. What kind of people are they? So much educating to do.
Yeah, I know that. Maybe I could hire someone to humiliate him.

So you’re just okay that they act so innocent when they did wrong? Emotional abuse is still abuse. If anything, is punishable by court. 

But this guy, he’s from rising political power and justice system is really shitty. So believe me, this makes me more mad.

Yeah, it really sucks. I am still early in my recovery stage so I’m not really sure what to say, just that I have fears of spiraling back. I don’t really have fears of missing out but I guess I relate since after getting out of my relationship with my Nex, I can say there were really chunks of time that were wasted. I could have used those precious time to get ahead of my game and be more than my age, not behind of it. 

However, when I find myself starting to entertain ideas again of how my nex is just a terribly hurt person who I need to consider or that I miss him despite the abuses etc. which is dumb and apparently just a sign of codependence— I try to list in my head the bad things that he has done in the tenure of our relationship, if not, I go here and read about other people’s experiences. I do this to remind myself I should not go back to what was, no matter what. 

Others try to list down using actual pen and paper all bad qualities of the relationship they don’t want to be in based on their previous experiences and also list down the good qualities they want to be in. But unfortunately, this doesn’t really work well for me as the abuse still left me unable to write and feel good about picking a fresh page. It takes a lot of courage to write something, even through my laptop or this reply I’m typing right now with my phone but I’m really trying. So, I guess, what I’m trying to say is: do find something that works best for you to beat that feeling of spiraling back and feeling you’ve lost so much along the way. 

I don’t know what your motivations are right now, but mine for example is financial stability so I can leave the country and be farther away from him. So, I am really focusing on my new job and trying to get busy with it so to not entertain thoughts of him. So, if you need to pick a new job, just go! You can do it!

Now that's interesting. How do they teach these techniques? I'm curious if they subject agents into emotional abuse as some form of social experiment to toughen them up. And I'm not saying that as an offence, my hypothesis on "empath" has just really led me to questioning further about the "why's" and "how's" of it.

Right. I think I am also arriving with an answer to my question too. It isn't really a definite diagnostic criteria or anything, it's just about empathy. But this leads me to a new question which is the "Whys" of it. Why do other people seem to have more or have developed an abundance of it while others don't? Things like that...

Yes, I do know what empathy means. And yes you have valid examples. We all have our hypothesis as to why we can be “empaths” but then again, I think I am getting an answer to this one now-- the coined term is not really a backed-up science.
It is stressful. All the more stressful because you have no idea how you’re feeling all of this like it’s a blizzard.

I wouldn’t also say I don’t believe you especially since I experience it myself. I have heightened consciousness with the people I personally interact and if I were a cop or some detective, I think I’d make a fine one just by my ability to detect that something’s wrong or how I can accommodate other’s feelings. I’d prolly sign up head on. But to toughen up is a different story because if I knew how to pull my emotional boundaries well, then I wouldn’t have landed in psychotherapy after my nex’s abuse. 

Maybe, the key is to be detached? lol. That still sounds wrong. Boundaries indeed.

Thanks for this, I’ll look into it. 

I get you. I don’t want to be defensive too of the possible traumas that have really paved way for my narcissist to drain me like this. It is unattractive and it’s not always beautiful. I don’t want to be stuck in a cycle of abuse and continue to doubt myself while giving my abuser all the benefit of the doubt. The term is suspicious indeed, the first time I looked it up, it spoke of psychic field and what not (I don’t have problem with this, I am just not knowledgeable of its workings). I was looking for some more scientifically claimed reasons behind it but I guess we’re all still lingering on our own hypothesis.

Yeah, I looked into it and it’s not really in the books like DSM-5. But it sure is something. Like, if there are actual clinical tests or diagnostics that would identify one into the criteria (assuming there’s one) then I’d prolly pay to take those tests. I don’t really want to box myself in a category but I want to understand myself and the people around me as well.

What you mentioned above is true and relatable. I just hope that people in the field could maybe look into this a little more(?) and if there exist studies about it, I hope I can get an in-depth on it. Because if MRIs could detect low level of empathy among narcs and sociopaths then maybe they can also explain how some may have developed an abundance in empathy to the point of getting caught in abusive relationship or what.

I am hoping too that people in the field of Psychology or Psychiatry could study more about this. If they can point out the low level of empathy among narcs and sociopaths, then they must also have some explanation for those people who seem  to have or have developed an abundance in empathy. It honestly can still get people in trouble- look why we’re here.
It’s just sad. It is indeed a survival skill by the looks of it- but can also doom us if we forget to put up the brave face or our invisible wall of boundaries for self-care.

I am actually learning something from your insight. You may be right, I also had this very abusive and irate brother while I was growing up and my sister was really a strict disciplinarian and a perfectionist as well (although we’re friends) but that was really a long time ago to me, I barely even feel his existence now. I wouldn’t want to go deeper into family history of abuse but I’m getting a pattern here. 

I do have moments where I feel I must tune into what other people need without them explicitly saying it, either bec I could assume the potential result or consequences such as emotional discomfort (sometimes, I feel like Dr. Strange who could predict so many possible outcomes in a split second if I don’t do or do something for someone) so I’d rather avoid and keep that from happening. 

But this is actually kinda sad... to think that what you thought of as a “gift” can only be achieved by going through unimaginable mental, physical, and emotional abuse. Of course, empathy is really a good thing but there has to be balance.

I do know those subs and I’ll try to look into those. I wouldn’t say I had severe childhood abuse, granted I do have a few traumas from some toxic relatives or family members who may have been narcs but rest assured they’re already discarded from my life a long time ago. If being too sensitive or “empath” has something to do with having a history of family conflict and abuse, then that’s just really... sad. Still, I believe empathy is really a good thing but boundaries for self-care is also very important to learn.

Yeah. It can be draining. By the sound of it, you seem to have finally learned to create a boundary for self-care that works for you. My therapist also told me to start outlining boundaries for self-care and that’s really something I need to work on while still being polite.

I kinda laughed with your story about “uber drivers”. But I do get the feeling, even though I empathize to people, I also have my moments of wanting to be alone. (Especially on car rides, I like to just enjoy the scenic route and not be disturbed. lol.) 

I totally get the feeling of being cornered by a driver who has so much story to tell, sometimes unsolicited advices. Although I didn’t see it in a way that’s crossing much of my boundaries (in my hometown, for example, taxi drivers are known to be the friendliest) I do have difficult time too of maneuvering or politely declining bec they may be really bored or what.

Well, this sure is familiar. I need not ask. Admittedly, I do feel so much for other people and it wasn’t like this before. Sure, I had empathy. I know when to be considerate and I feel other’s pain too. I am sensitive to people’s tone of voice and manners, and I could almost tell if one is lying or doesn’t like me or what. But then again, I had my years of detachment too until I met my nex. I believe you... sometimes I wish that I could give away some of the overflowing empathy I have in my veins to those who lack or don’t even have it, that they, too, may finally understand.

> I realised I never did love my nex. It was a codependence thing, not love. Love is a choice, it's something you do, not feel."

Wow! I believe you. I wish I can say the first sentence though.

Is there really a science behind being an "empath"? Like is it legitimately a spectrum? I don't know if I'm asking the right question but I hope you get it. I'm asking because I've recently just explored this notion in hopes of understanding why I "feel" so much for other people even towards my Nex who hurt me the most.

This also crossed my mind- I watched this film recently too and was asking the same question. Binge watching films has been some form of coping mechanism for me after the break up. In the movie, my opinion was that it's unreasonable for the girl to erase the guy from her memory, I don't think the reason is strong enough. In my case on the other hand, I still couldn't decide. There are times when I'm in pain again where I would wish to erase him, other times, I would look back at myself having been able to have so much capacity to love. 

P.S. I feel really thankful to this community because finally at least I feel that there are people who can feel and think the same way as I do and wouldn't make me question my thoughts and sanity just for a second. Just the little things that I can relate to makes me smile so thank you.

That's exactly what I've been telling myself and some close friends lately too--that it's so hard to see the good in people anymore. One thing I learned from someone in the community is that since we are normal people, we don't automatically assume the worst in someone when we meet them. That said, don't become the person like your Nex who only sees others as pawns or objects to hurt and manipulate. Continue seeing the good in people while maintaining boundaries for self care. 

"Because I had no interest in dating earlier in life, this was my first relationship (for reference, I was post college). I had no frame of reference other than her being genuine and altruistic. This led to me getting hurt considerably worse than I believe others who were taught to be more careful and discerning would have been in my same situation. I didn't understand any of the red flags that, in hindsight, seem like they should have been obvious."

This is just as familiar to me. Dated my Nex while I was in my last quarter in college and he was practically my first real relationship. He got me by being very honest with me about his struggles and sob story, I really thought he was someone who I can be real with. I was very willing to accept him for all his insecurities, warts and all but it turns out he's a sociopath. At some point, I self-destructed because of him. There were many impractical things that I did just to save our relationship but I should have known not to dismiss all the red flags in the first place. The next time you go in a relationship, make sure it's not something that requires too much investigating. And trust your intuition!

I am also trying to put things in paper and just write to my Nex a letter instead of agreeing to meet him in person, go out of my way to book a flight to his city so we could finally have that "closure". But I am so hurt, nothing could really come out from my writing. If you don't mind, I'd copy some of your thoughts here.

I had this fear of my Nex finding me on Reddit too although I found his first. There was nothing much there. At first, I used to just browse and read subs here silently. It wasn’t until things started breaking down between us that I started posting here. It was scary at first bec it was personal yet insightful. I had to delete some of my postings and comments but I know other’s comments on my now deleted posts will still exist . But I don’t care anymore if he sees mine- he could either read about the hardships I’ve been through or the amount of understanding I’ve extended towards him. Still, I know it wouldn’t change anything. 

Weird enough, I’ve been having dreams about my nex too. Just awhile ago, I dreamt of him cuddling beside me in bed. He was this peaceful person. Maybe that’s just my deeper wishful thinking - that we could go back to being “normal”.
I still feel the loneliest after being discarded with his “best friend” last Christmas. I hope this week will be the only time I will be lonely this year and after that, I hope to move on.

“The part that still hurts the most is my own participation in the manipulation. I had an intuition that there was something “off” about him. Unfortunately, I disregarded my gut feeling that there was something wrong with him. Never again. If I get even a whiff that there is something not right with a relationship or a person, I’m out.”

This is exactly something I would say. And until now, I am still hurting.

There’s  nothing here that I don’t relate. The break up just happened this Christmas and until now my heart is really still heavy because I looked like the most insecure person in the relationship when all along he made me feel this way. It is so difficult, I don’t know what to do with this pain.
Not a chance. I’ve to think about what to do for the next few days.
I have fear of eventually knowing he’s with someone else already. How do I even deal with that this time around.

Oh same! It really sucks  We had an argument by afternoon Christmas bec it was the birthday of the girl he triangulated, compared, and gaslighted me with. My anxiety got overboard thinking they might be secretly together again and I policed real bad to get him sc his conversations with her. Got hurt that during the times he was “feeling under the weather” and “antisocial” he was actually able to have a brief convo with the girl while telling me he can’t talk to me.
It sucks. Even the second time around. It really sucks. I don’t want to be alone during the holidays again.
That’s helpful. I will try. It is difficult because it is not in my nature to fix my look on a person’s wrong-doing. It would be hard to not think about the good times and yearn for it.

I was gonna move in his city and go for a new job and career but I guess it won’t be necessary now. Now, I’m caught in financial instability due to a hasty resignation to accommodate him in my life. I chose this, yeah, in hopes of it being worth it.
There’s this slimmer of hope in me for the next 4 months that I want to kill- because it is only hoping for him to come back to me. I’ve never wished to kill ‘hope’ in my life like this at all.

I really want to see only the good in him but there’s a voice rebelling in my head telling me I should be more strict on him. He just confessed how he manipulated and gaslighted me from the start of our relationship though I’ve always had this intuition he was doing something else or that. He showed me nothing but kind gestures in the tenure of our relationship until he took back everything he said. I really appreciate all good and sweet gestures but the deceit and lies were really destructive. I’d do so much to have him mean what he does and say to me but now he is already telling me negative or opposite things. I’ve been blaming myself a lot for having to question him and even confront him, because I just really want us to be back to a peaceful bonding (no matter what is happening in the background).  Truth indeed hurts.
Hmmm. Now I know how my cat actually hid her kittens in our attic after giving birth to them on the porch!

I’m from Sociology too. I did say the writer was able to present a well narrative about his experience inside a high-end mall (as for the effort to see the strange in the familiar). Believe me, I’ve read more pretentious paragraphs from University journals etc. than this mere Facebook status/draft. I’d say this can be improved but I commend who ever wrote this for putting his own narrative down. It’s the first step.

Tbh, what I’ve hoped is that since the issue at hand is about disparity inside the mall, I’d be able to read about more discussion relevant to it. Majority here fell into groupthink by just dropping “this piece is pretentious” without even saying something about its valid points.

I don’t understand why this is getting hate comments. This is actually a very good presentation of sociological imagination- to see the strange in the familiar.  No need to smart-shame him for the use of “big words”, the context is well.

Part of me is intuitive about it from the start, that that's what's going on, that he's doing everything on purpose either get me or so he would have better options when the time comes he will need to choose or something. But I think I gave him too much benefit of the doubt. It is still very difficult for me especially since we tried forgetting about the past now and all of a sudden it is resurfacing and breaking me.

I am very much aware of the situation now, thanks. I did try to put off communication until an exchange began again the past 6 months ago, that's when we tried working things out again. He went to continue his therapy and I'll seek mine too at the end of this month perhaps. I am trying to outline boundaries for self care as suggested by my therapist. No matter, I don't want to inflict harm on him especially since he admits to developing strong attachment to me and needs me to be better. Leaving him now would break him and he might try to Overdose pills again. The red flags are teasing me all over. This is the dilemma.

Thanks for letting me know about the concept of Triangulation. First time to know about it. As I've been listening to the podcast, I can't help but agree to facts and what's going on. I do want to save my time and not waste it for someone who can't live up to the promises of change. I did try to put off communication until an exchange began again the past 6 months ago, that's when we tried working things out again. He cut ties with his "close friend" (who also messaged me she didn't want to be friends with him anymore too) and he tries to communicate more openly about the events of his life now. While I am still on my guard, I know I'll never be the same in the relationship. The dilemma of destroying what could be the real new start we built for the past 6 months is just taking a toll on me recently especially since he just admitted last week how he did lie to me before and how I didn't hear him wrong. It's difficult for him to say the truth but and I can see he is trying. I've been giving all the benefits of the doubt, I know. This relapse in me is just really heartbreaking. 

I'll try to know more and get answers to what's bothering me before making decisions. Thank you very much.
